Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim - Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator (QEMU functional + vsim cycle-accurate, two-phase handoff QEMU1 -> vsim).
CANONICAL docs that are the source of truth and MUST be kept (do not recommend deleting these): CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md (always-current user guide), docs/FRS.md, docs/MRD.md, ROADMAP.md (master FR tracker, "single source of truth"), driver/ROADMAP.md (C++ andes-sim driver tracker), docs/engine_interface.md, docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb (the L-id capability-gap envelope).
The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `gemm_modes.md`

Steps:
1. Read `gemm_modes.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

4	> removed; the four switching modes are now reachable via
5	> `./hsim run --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint` directly. This file is kept
6	> as a record of the design decisions (one workload, two builds, why).
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	Every switching mode should showcase its mechanism on the SAME
11	RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
12	modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (whose profile / per-phase drain /
13	archive stages live inside `./hsim run --mode simpoint`).
14	
15	We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,
16	`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).
17	
18	## Why two builds of one source
19	
20	`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
21	matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
22	marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:
23	
24	- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
25	- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.
26	
27	Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.
28	
29	### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
30	- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
31	  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.
32	  Fix: mark `vmatmul_kernel` `noinline` (also keeps it in the ROI per
33	  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).
34	- Orchestrator CSR-drain is marker-driven: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py:33` passes
35	  the plugin only `outfile=...`; `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:237` sets replay
36	  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

45	| simpoint | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |

   "source": "### L23. mscratch (M-mode software scratch CSR) did not round-trip  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bit: any bare-metal, trap-free, single-privilege ROI -- the
  envelope cell-5 calls *supported* -- that used `mscratch` (CSR 0x340)
  across the handoff. `mscratch` is the M-mode software scratch register, a
  side-effect-free read/write CSR; using it needs no trap, no interrupt,
  no paging. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never
  re-read at drain, so:
  1. a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value

  2. a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the drained state,

   "source": "### L25. ROI code that reads or writes time-variant CSRs produces engine-dependent results  (new 2026-06-15)

- **The rule**: code inside the ROI must treat `mcycle` (0xB00), `minstret`
  (0xB02), `mip` (0x344), and `time` (0xC01) as opaque.  No branches,
  arithmetic, or writes on these CSRs inside the ROI.
- **Why**: QEMU approximates both cycle and instruction counts with a CPI≈1
  model; vsim counts actual RTL pipeline cycles and retires.  `mip` pending
  bits (MTIP, MEIP, MSIP) reflect live timer/platform state that differs
  between QEMU's functional clock and vsim's cycle clock.  These values
  diverge at every architectural moment inside the ROI -- by construction,
  not by bug.
- **What happens if the rule is broken**:
  - *Branch on `mcycle`/`minstret`*: the `--verify` oracle (pure QEMU)
    takes a different branch than the hybrid run (vsim); the diff reports a
    GPR or PC mismatch.  The plain run passes; only `--verify` exposes it.

    counter): `StateDrain` re-reads the reset value at the exit marker; the
    reported cycle delta is near-zero or underflows -- silently wrong.

  between the entry and exit markers.

  delta), `tests/fixtures/break_verify_diverge.S` (branch diverges under
  `--verify`).

  DV path; L25 is about the hybrid measurement path and any code that reads
  or modifies time-variant state inside the ROI.
- **Status**: by design.  A static linter on the ELF could warn on in-ROI
  reads/writes of these CSRs (not built)."

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./andes-sim`
35	
36	`./andes-sim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
37	self-builds on first use). It wraps the developer-grade scripts
38	documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`, `tests/e2e.sh`,
39	`scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind a few subcommands.
40	
41	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
42	
43	```sh
44	./andes-sim build                                       # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
45	./andes-sim list engines                                # discover the built engines
46	./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
47	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one CSR-trigger handoff
48	./andes-sim test                                        # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
49	```
50	
51	Expected last line of `./andes-sim test`:
52	
53	```
54	PASS 45, FAIL 0, SKIP 0 (elapsed: <Ns>)
55	```
56	
57	Subcommand cheat sheet:
58	
59	| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
60	|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
61	| `./andes-sim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
62	| `./andes-sim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                  | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`, `runtime`. |
63	| `./andes-sim run --model fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc|icount] [--engine ID] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff). |
64	| `./andes-sim test [--filter REGEX] [--mode marker|pc|both] [--jobs N]` | Run the e2e suite; defaults `--mode both --jobs 8`.              |
65	
66	Run `./andes-sim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
67	`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` to see the developer commands). The SimPoint pipeline
68	(`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`,
69	`replay`) still lives in the Python reference driver `./hsim.py` until
70	the C++ port lands. The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
71	underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andes-sim`
72	(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).
